whatsHappening.background: The Central African Republic has endured decades of coups, armed conflict, and weak state control. The crisis deepened after Seleka rebels seized Bangui in 2013 and anti-Balaka militias formed in response, setting off years of violence, displacement, and insecurity. Although peace agreements and elections followed, armed groups still control large parts of the country and civilians continue to live with instability, fear, and extremely weak public services.

parties.name: Government of CAR
parties.description: The national government and army have tried to hold state control and fight armed groups, often with limited reach outside Bangui.

parties.name: Seleka
parties.description: A mainly Muslim rebel coalition that captured Bangui in 2013 and removed President François Bozizé from power.

parties.name: ex-Seleka Groups
parties.description: Smaller armed factions that emerged after Seleka splintered and continued fighting in different parts of the country.

parties.name: anti-Balaka
parties.description: Mainly Christian militias formed in response to Seleka violence but also carried out revenge attacks against Muslim civilians.

parties.name: CPC
parties.description: A coalition of six armed groups that attacked the government around the 2020 to 2021 elections.

parties.name: MINUSCA and Foreign Forces
parties.description: The UN peacekeeping mission MINUSCA, along with Rwandan soldiers and Russian Wagner-linked forces, have helped support the government against rebels.

timeline.description: François Bozizé takes power in a coup while rebel violence and poverty remain widespread.
Seleka captures Bangui and removes Bozizé, triggering a new phase of national crisis.
The UN creates MINUSCA to protect civilians and help stabilize the country.
The government and 14 armed groups sign a peace agreement, but it is not fully implemented.
The CPC attacks again, threatening Bangui before government forces push back with outside military support.

civilianImpact.experiences: Civilians in the Central African Republic live with recurring violence, forced displacement, disrupted schooling, weak public services, and severe poverty. Humanitarian needs remain extremely high, especially for children. Many communities still struggle to access clean water, education, and basic safety as repeated conflict keeps families trapped in long-term instability.

image.alt: Civilians in the Central African Republic affected by displacement and humanitarian crisis

howToHelp.summary: The Central African Republic receives far less global attention than many other crises, even though humanitarian needs remain severe. Raising awareness and supporting organizations already working on the ground can help families access protection, shelter, education, and essential services.

learnMore.text: This slide introduces how repeated coups, militia violence, and failed peace efforts created today’s crisis in the Central African Republic.

whatsHappening.background: The conflict in the Central African Republic is not only military. It is also a humanitarian crisis shaped by displacement, poverty, disrupted education, and weak access to water and essential services. Children and families in remote regions are often the most affected.

parties.name: 2.3 million people in need

parties.name: 1.2 million children affected
parties.description: Children make up a major portion of those in need of urgent support.

parties.name: Families forced from home
parties.description: Over 1.4 million people have been forcibly displaced by violence and insecurity.

parties.name: Communities without basic services
parties.description: Many areas lack reliable access to school, safe water, and stable protection.

civilianImpact.experiences: For many civilians, the crisis means children missing school, families lacking clean water, and communities living with displacement and economic hardship. Years of conflict have weakened already fragile systems, leaving millions dependent on humanitarian support while violence and poverty continue to reinforce one another.

image.alt: Humanitarian needs and poverty in the Central African Republic

howToHelp.summary: Humanitarian needs in the Central African Republic remain severe because conflict, displacement, and poverty keep basic services out of reach for many communities. Relief efforts help, but under-attention makes sustained support even more important.

learnMore.text: The civilian toll includes displacement, interrupted education, weak infrastructure, and severe poverty across much of the country.

whatsHappening.background: Support is most effective when it goes to organizations already working in the Central African Republic and when it helps raise awareness about a crisis that is often overlooked. Even public attention can matter because underreported crises often struggle to attract sustained aid.

parties.name: UNICEF
parties.description: Supports children and families with health, nutrition, education, water, and protection services.

parties.name: UNHCR
parties.description: Supports displaced people and refugees with protection, shelter, and humanitarian assistance.

parties.name: Humanitarian Awareness
parties.description: Sharing verified information helps bring attention to a crisis that often receives too little global focus.

civilianImpact.experiences: Helping the Central African Republic means responding to a crisis that is both severe and underreported. Donations can support children, displaced families, education, water access, and protection services, while awareness helps prevent the crisis from being ignored.

image.alt: Families in the Central African Republic affected by crisis

howToHelp.summary: Share information about the Central African Republic so the crisis is not forgotten, and donate to organizations such as UNICEF or UNHCR that are already working there. Public awareness and direct support both matter in places where humanitarian need is high but global attention is low.

learnMore.text: Follow crisis updates from UNICEF, UNHCR, and other verified humanitarian sources to stay informed and support trusted relief efforts.
